facts.title: Capital of Australia
facts.statement: Canberra is the capital of Australia. It was purpose-built from 1913 as a compromise after Sydney and Melbourne both refused to let the other have it.
facts.question: What is the capital of Australia?
facts.hook: Neither rival would yield, so Australia built a brand-new capital in the gap between them.

facts.title: Capital of Canada
facts.statement: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, chosen by Queen Victoria in 1857 partly because it sat on the border between English and French Canada.
facts.question: What is the capital of Canada?
facts.hook: Not Toronto, not Montreal — a border-town compromise, the same story as Canberra.

facts.title: Capital of Brazil
facts.statement: Brasília is the capital of Brazil. It was built from empty savannah in just 41 months and inaugurated in 1960 to pull development inland from the coast.
facts.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
facts.hook: Laid out in the shape of an aeroplane, and less than 70 years old.

facts.title: Capital of Turkey
facts.statement: Ankara is the capital of Turkey. Atatürk moved the capital there from Istanbul in 1923 to anchor the new republic in the Anatolian heartland.
facts.question: What is the capital of Turkey?
facts.hook: Istanbul is the famous one; Ankara is the working one.

facts.title: Capital of Switzerland
facts.statement: Bern is the de facto capital of Switzerland. The Swiss constitution avoids the word 'capital', calling Bern the federal city instead.
facts.question: What is the capital of Switzerland?
facts.hook: Not Zurich and not Geneva — Switzerland deliberately gave the honour to a smaller city.

facts.title: Capital of New Zealand
facts.statement: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, and the southernmost capital city of any sovereign state in the world.
facts.question: What is the capital of New Zealand?
facts.hook: Auckland is bigger; Wellington governs.

facts.title: Capital of Nigeria
facts.statement: Abuja is the capital of Nigeria. It replaced Lagos in 1991 because it sat centrally, on neutral ground between the country's major ethnic regions.
facts.question: What is the capital of Nigeria?
facts.hook: Lagos is the megacity; Abuja is the neutral centre.
facts.details:
Abuja () is the capital city of Nigeria, strategically situated at the geographic midpoint of the country within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). As the seat of the Federal Government of Nigeria, it hosts key national institutions, landmarks, and buildings spread across its over 50 districts. It replaced Lagos (the most populous city in Nigeria) as the capital on 12 December 1991.
Abuja's geography is defined by Aso Rock, a 400-metre (1,300 ft) monolith left by water erosion. The Presidential Complex, National Assembly, Supreme Court, and much of the city extends to the south of the rock. Zuma Rock, a 725-metre (2,379 ft) monolith, lies just north of the city on the expressway to Kaduna.
At the 2006 census, the city of Abuja had a population of 776,298 and 179,674 households, making it one of the ten most populous cities in Nigeria (eighth place in 2006). According to the United Nations, Abuja grew by 139.7% between 2000 and 2010, making it the fastest-growing city in the world. As of 2015, the city is experiencing an annual growth of at least 35%, retaining its position as the fastest-growing city on the African continent and one of the fastest-growing in the world.
Major religious sites include the Nigerian National Mosque and the Nigerian National Christian Centre.

facts.title: Capital of Myanmar
facts.statement: Naypyidaw is the capital of Myanmar. The military government moved there abruptly in 2005, building a vast, famously empty city with 20-lane highways.
facts.question: What is the capital of Myanmar?
facts.hook: A capital built for millions that almost nobody lives in.
facts.details:
Naypyidaw ( NAYP-yid-aw), officially romanised as Nay Pyi Taw (NPT), is the capital and third-largest city of Myanmar. The city is located at the centre of the Naypyidaw Union Territory. It is unusual among Myanmar's cities in that it is an entirely planned city and not part of any state or region. The city, previously known only as Pyinmana District, officially replaced Yangon as the administrative capital of Myanmar on 6 November 2005; its official name was revealed to the public on Armed Forces Day, 27 March 2006.
As the seat of the government of Myanmar, Naypyidaw is the site of the Assembly of the Union, the Supreme Court, the Presidential Palace, the official residences of the Cabinet and the headquarters of government ministries and military. Naypyidaw is notable for its unusual combination of large size and very low population density. The city hosted the 24th and 25th ASEAN Summit, the 3rd BIMSTEC Summit, the Ninth East Asia Summit, the 2013 Southeast Asian Games and the 2014 AFC U-19 Championship.


== Etymology ==
Naypyidaw is Burmese for "abode of the king", and is generally translated as "royal capital", "seat of the king", or "abode of kings". Traditionally, it was used as a suffix to the names of royal capitals, such as Mandalay, which was called Yadanabon Naypyidaw (ရတနာပုံနေပြည်တော်).


== History ==
Naypyidaw was founded on a greenfield site near Pyinmana, about 320 kilometres (200 mi) north of the old capital, Yangon.

facts.title: Capital of Kazakhstan
facts.statement: Astana is the capital of Kazakhstan. It was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and then changed back to Astana in 2022.
facts.question: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
facts.hook: 'Astana' simply means 'capital city' in Kazakh.

facts.title: Capital of Morocco
facts.statement: Rabat is the capital of Morocco, though Casablanca is considerably larger and better known abroad.
facts.question: What is the capital of Morocco?
facts.hook: Casablanca got the film; Rabat got the government.

facts.title: Capital of Vietnam
facts.statement: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam. Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon, is the larger commercial centre in the south.
facts.question: What is the capital of Vietnam?
facts.hook: The north governs, the south trades.

facts.title: Capital of Pakistan
facts.statement: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan, purpose-built in the 1960s to replace Karachi.
facts.question: What is the capital of Pakistan?
facts.hook: Karachi is the port and the giant; Islamabad was designed to govern.

facts.title: South Africa's three capitals
facts.statement: South Africa splits its capital functions across three cities: Pretoria is the executive capital, Cape Town the legislative, and Bloemfontein the judicial.
facts.question: Which city is the executive (administrative) capital of South Africa?
facts.hook: Three branches, three cities — a deliberate post-union compromise.

facts.title: Bolivia's constitutional capital
facts.statement: Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia, while La Paz is the seat of government and home to the legislature.
facts.question: What is the constitutional capital of Bolivia?
facts.hook: La Paz governs day to day; Sucre holds the title on paper.

facts.title: Capital of Tanzania
facts.statement: Dodoma is the official capital of Tanzania, chosen for its central position, though Dar es Salaam remains the largest city.
facts.question: What is the capital of Tanzania?
facts.hook: Another 'move inland to the middle' capital.

facts.title: Capital of Ivory Coast
facts.statement: Yamoussoukro is the official capital of Ivory Coast — the birthplace of its first president — while Abidjan remains the economic centre.
facts.question: What is the official capital of Ivory Coast?
facts.hook: A president promoted his own home village to capital.

facts.title: Capital of Belize
facts.statement: Belmopan is the capital of Belize. The government moved inland after Hurricane Hattie devastated coastal Belize City in 1961.
facts.question: What is the capital of Belize?
facts.hook: A hurricane wrote this one: the capital fled the coast.

facts.title: Capital of Sri Lanka
facts.statement: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the official capital of Sri Lanka, a suburb of Colombo, which remains the commercial capital.
facts.question: What is the official capital of Sri Lanka?
facts.hook: Colombo is the answer most people give — and it is the wrong one.
facts.details:
Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (Sinhala pronunciation: [ʃriː dʒajəʋard̪ənəpurə ko̞ːʈːe̞ː]), also known as Kotte, is the legislative capital city of Sri Lanka. Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is located adjacent to the urban area of Sri Lanka's de facto economic capital, Colombo.
The Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte Municipal Council area is bounded in:

the North by Kolonnawa Urban Council area,
the North-East by the Kotikawatta–Mulleriyawa Pradeshiya Sabha area,
the East by the Kaduwela Municipal Council area,
the South-East by the Maharagama Urban Council area,
the South-West by the Dehiwala-Mount Lavinia Municipal Council and
the West by the Colombo Municipal Council area, which is the commercial capital of Sri Lanka.


== History ==

The village of Darugama lay at the confluence of two streams, the Diyawanna Oya and the Kolonnawa Oya. As Darugama was a naturally secure place, it was not easy for enemies to enter it. Here, in the 13th century, a local chieftain, Nissanka Alagakkonara, built a Kotte, or fortress.
Alagakkonara is mentioned by Ibn Batuta as ruling in Kurunegala, but other sources indicate that he was the Bandara (Guardian) of Raigama Korale (county) in the modern Kalutara District. Arya Chakravarthy's army was held by Alagakkonara in front of Kotte, while he defeated the enemy's invasion fleet at Panadura to the south-west.
Kotte was a jala durgha (water fortress), in the shape of a triangle, with the Diyawanna Oya and Kolonnawa Oya marshes forming two long sides; along the shorter third (land) side a large moat (the 'inner moat') was dug. The fortress was nearly 2.5 km2 (0.97 sq mi) in area, fortified with ramparts of kabook or laterite rock, 2.5 metres (8 ft 2 in) high and 10.7 metres (35 ft) in breadth.

facts.title: Capital of Malaysia
facts.statement: Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia, though the federal administrative centre moved to nearby Putrajaya in the late 1990s.
facts.question: What is the capital of Malaysia?

facts.title: Capital of the Netherlands
facts.statement: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands, but the government, parliament and royal residence are all in The Hague.
facts.question: What is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands?
facts.hook: The Hague does the governing; Amsterdam keeps the title.

facts.title: Capital of Portugal
facts.statement: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal and one of the oldest cities in Western Europe, predating London, Paris and Rome as a settlement.
facts.question: What is the capital of Portugal?

facts.title: Capital of Argentina
facts.statement: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina. Its residents are called porteños — 'people of the port'.
facts.question: What is the capital of Argentina?
facts.details:
Buenos Aires, officially the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, is the capital and largest city of Argentina. It is located on the southwest of the Río de la Plata. Buenos Aires is classified as an Alpha− global city, according to the GaWC 2024 ranking. The city proper has a population of 3.1 million and its urban area has a population of 16.7 million, making it the 21st most populous metropolitan area in the world.
It is known for its preserved eclectic European architecture and rich cultural life. It is a multicultural city that is home to multiple ethnic and religious groups, contributing to its culture as well as to the dialect spoken in the city and in other parts of the country. Since the 19th century, the city, and the country in general, has been a major recipient of millions of immigrants from all over the world, making it a melting pot where many ethnic groups live together. Buenos Aires is considered one of the most diverse cities of the Americas.
The city of Buenos Aires is an autonomous district and is neither part of Buenos Aires Province nor its capital. In 1880, after the Argentine Civil War, Buenos Aires was federalized and split from Buenos Aires Province.

facts.title: Capital of India
facts.statement: New Delhi is the capital of India. The British moved the capital there from Calcutta in 1911 and built the new city alongside old Delhi.
facts.question: What is the capital of India?
facts.hook: Delhi is the metropolis; New Delhi is the planned district inside it that governs.

facts.title: Capital of Egypt
facts.statement: Cairo is the capital of Egypt and the largest city in the Arab world.
facts.question: What is the capital of Egypt?

facts.title: Capital of Norway
facts.statement: Oslo is the capital of Norway. It was called Christiania, after the Danish king, from 1624 until 1925.
facts.question: What is the capital of Norway?

facts.title: Largest country by area
facts.statement: Russia is by far the largest country on Earth at about 17 million square kilometres — roughly an eighth of all inhabited land, and nearly twice the size of Canada.
facts.question: Which is the largest country in the world by land area?

facts.title: Most populous country
facts.statement: India overtook China in 2023 to become the world's most populous country, with over 1.4 billion people.
facts.question: Which country has the largest population in the world?
facts.hook: The answer changed in 2023 — for decades it was China.

facts.title: Longest coastline
facts.statement: Canada has the longest coastline of any country — over 200,000 km, thanks to its vast Arctic archipelago.
facts.question: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
facts.hook: Not the biggest country, but the most raggedly edged one.

facts.title: Smallest country
facts.statement: Vatican City is the smallest sovereign state in the world, covering about 0.49 square kilometres inside Rome.
facts.question: What is the smallest country in the world?
facts.hook: You can walk across the whole country in about ten minutes.

facts.title: Country surrounded by South Africa
facts.statement: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa — one of only three countries in the world entirely enclosed by a single other state.
facts.question: Which country is entirely surrounded by South Africa?
facts.hook: The other two enclaves are San Marino and Vatican City, both inside Italy.

facts.title: Country with the most time zones
facts.statement: France has the most time zones of any country — twelve — because of its overseas territories spread across every ocean.
facts.question: Which country spans the most time zones?
facts.hook: Russia looks like the obvious answer, but France's island territories beat it.

facts.title: Machu Picchu's country
facts.statement: Machu Picchu, the 15th-century Inca citadel, sits high in the Andes of Peru.
facts.question: In which country is Machu Picchu?

facts.title: Kilimanjaro's country
facts.statement: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak, stands in northeastern Tanzania near the Kenyan border.
facts.question: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro?
facts.hook: It is visible from Kenya, which is why so many people guess wrong.

facts.title: Doubly landlocked in Europe
facts.statement: Liechtenstein is doubly landlocked — every country bordering it is itself landlocked. Uzbekistan is the only other example on Earth.
facts.question: Which European country is doubly landlocked?
facts.hook: You must cross two borders from Liechtenstein before you can reach the sea.

facts.title: Most populous landlocked country
facts.statement: Ethiopia is the world's most populous landlocked country, having lost its coastline when Eritrea became independent in 1993.
facts.question: What is the most populous landlocked country in the world?

facts.title: The only country that is a continent
facts.statement: Australia is the only country that occupies an entire continent, and it is also the world's largest island by the usual reckoning.
facts.question: Which country occupies an entire continent by itself?

facts.title: Country with the most islands
facts.statement: Sweden has more islands than any other country — around 270,000, though only a few thousand are inhabited.
facts.question: Which country has the most islands?
facts.hook: Indonesia and the Philippines feel like the answer; Sweden's tiny Baltic skerries win it.

facts.title: Longest river
facts.statement: The Nile, flowing about 6,650 km north through eleven countries into the Mediterranean, is traditionally considered the world's longest river.
facts.question: Which is traditionally considered the longest river in the world?
facts.hook: It flows north, which trips people up — rivers have no obligation to run 'down' the map.

facts.title: River with the greatest discharge
facts.statement: The Amazon carries more water than any other river — roughly a fifth of all river water reaching the oceans, more than the next seven rivers combined.
facts.question: Which river discharges the most water into the ocean?
facts.hook: Longest is disputed; biggest by volume is not even close.

facts.title: Longest river in Europe
facts.statement: The Volga is Europe's longest river, running about 3,530 km through Russia into the Caspian Sea.
facts.question: What is the longest river in Europe?

facts.title: Longest river in Asia
facts.statement: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia and the third longest in the world, running about 6,300 km across China.
facts.question: What is the longest river in Asia?

facts.title: The river of Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade
facts.statement: The Danube flows through more countries than any other river — ten — and passes four national capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade.
facts.question: Which river flows through Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade?
facts.hook: Four capitals on one river — no other river manages more than one.

facts.title: Deepest river
facts.statement: The Congo is the world's deepest river, reaching depths of over 220 metres, and the only major river to cross the equator twice.
facts.question: What is the deepest river in the world?

facts.title: The river through Paris
facts.statement: The Seine flows through Paris, dividing it into the Right Bank and Left Bank before reaching the English Channel at Le Havre.
facts.question: Which river flows through Paris?

facts.title: The river through London
facts.statement: The Thames flows through London and is tidal as far inland as Teddington, about 90 km from the sea.
facts.question: Which river flows through London?

facts.title: Longest river in North America
facts.statement: The Missouri is the longest river in North America at about 3,770 km, slightly longer than the Mississippi it joins.
facts.question: What is the longest river in North America?
facts.hook: The Mississippi is the famous one; its tributary is the longer one.

facts.title: Highest mountain
facts.statement: Mount Everest is the highest point on Earth above sea level, at about 8,849 metres on the Nepal–China border.
facts.question: What is the highest mountain above sea level?

facts.title: Second-highest mountain
facts.statement: K2, on the China–Pakistan border, is the world's second-highest peak at 8,611 m and far deadlier to climb than Everest.
facts.question: What is the second-highest mountain in the world?
facts.hook: Its name is a survey code that simply stuck — Karakoram peak number 2.

facts.title: Highest mountain in Africa
facts.statement: Mount Kilimanjaro is Africa's highest mountain at 5,895 m, and the tallest freestanding mountain in the world.
facts.question: What is the highest mountain in Africa?

facts.title: Highest mountain outside Asia
facts.statement: Aconcagua in Argentina is the highest peak outside Asia at 6,961 m, and the highest in both the Southern and Western Hemispheres.
facts.question: What is the highest mountain outside Asia?

facts.title: Highest mountain in North America
facts.statement: Denali in Alaska is North America's highest peak at 6,190 m. It was officially named Mount McKinley until 2015.
facts.question: What is the highest mountain in North America?

facts.title: Highest peak in the Alps
facts.statement: Mont Blanc is the highest mountain in the Alps and in Western Europe, at about 4,808 m on the France–Italy border.
facts.question: What is the highest mountain in the Alps?

facts.title: Largest hot desert
facts.statement: The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth at about 9.2 million square kilometres — roughly the size of the United States.
facts.question: What is the largest hot desert in the world?

facts.title: Largest desert of any kind
facts.statement: Antarctica is the largest desert in the world. A desert is defined by precipitation, not heat, and Antarctica is the driest continent.
facts.question: What is the largest desert in the world?
facts.hook: Deserts are about rainfall, not sand — which makes the coldest place the biggest desert.

facts.title: Driest place on Earth
facts.statement: The Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest non-polar place on Earth; some weather stations there have never recorded rain.
facts.question: Which desert is the driest place on Earth outside the poles?

facts.title: The desert of Mongolia
facts.statement: The Gobi Desert spans southern Mongolia and northern China, and is famous for the first confirmed discovery of dinosaur eggs in 1923.
facts.question: Which desert covers southern Mongolia and northern China?

facts.title: Largest ocean
facts.statement: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about a third of the Earth's surface — more than all land combined.
facts.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?

facts.title: Smallest ocean
facts.statement: The Arctic is the smallest and shallowest of the world's oceans, much of it covered by sea ice.
facts.question: What is the smallest ocean?

facts.title: The second-largest ocean
facts.statement: The Atlantic is the second-largest ocean and is still widening by a few centimetres a year as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge pushes it apart.
facts.question: What is the second-largest ocean?

facts.title: The warmest ocean
facts.statement: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest and the warmest of the world's oceans, which drives the monsoon systems of South Asia.
facts.question: Which is the warmest of the world's oceans?

facts.title: Deepest point in the ocean
facts.statement: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific contains Challenger Deep, at about 10,935 m the deepest known point of any ocean.
facts.question: What is the deepest known place in the ocean?
facts.hook: Everest would sit inside it with more than two kilometres of water to spare.

facts.title: Lowest land on Earth
facts.statement: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest exposed land on Earth, roughly 430 m below sea level, and its water is nearly ten times saltier than the ocean.
facts.question: Which body of water lies at the lowest land elevation on Earth?

facts.title: The sea with no coastline
facts.statement: The Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic is the only sea on Earth with no land boundary — it is defined entirely by ocean currents.
facts.question: Which is the only sea with no coastline?
facts.hook: Its 'shores' are four currents rather than any land.

facts.title: Largest inland body of water
facts.statement: The Caspian Sea is the largest enclosed body of water on Earth — a lake by definition, though its size and salinity earned it the name 'sea'.
facts.question: What is the largest enclosed inland body of water in the world?

facts.title: The sea between Africa and Arabia
facts.statement: The Red Sea separates Africa from the Arabian Peninsula and links to the Mediterranean via the Suez Canal.
facts.question: Which sea separates Africa from the Arabian Peninsula?

facts.title: Deepest lake
facts.statement: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake on Earth at 1,642 m, and holds about a fifth of all the world's unfrozen fresh water.
facts.question: What is the deepest lake in the world?
facts.hook: One lake, a fifth of the planet's liquid fresh water.

facts.title: Largest freshwater lake by area
facts.statement: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area, one of North America's five Great Lakes.
facts.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?

facts.title: Largest lake in Africa
facts.statement: Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake and the chief reservoir of the Nile, shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.
facts.question: What is the largest lake in Africa?

facts.title: Highest navigable lake
facts.statement: Lake Titicaca, on the Peru–Bolivia border at 3,812 m, is the highest navigable lake in the world.
facts.question: What is the highest navigable lake in the world?

facts.title: Largest continent
facts.statement: Asia is the largest continent by both area and population, holding about 60% of humanity.
facts.question: What is the largest continent by area?

facts.title: Continent with the most countries
facts.statement: Africa contains 54 sovereign states, more than any other continent.
facts.question: Which continent has the most countries?

facts.title: The continent with no permanent residents
facts.statement: Antarctica has no permanent population, only rotating research staff, and is governed by the Antarctic Treaty of 1959.
facts.question: Which continent has no permanent human population?

facts.title: The continent crossed by the Equator, Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn
facts.statement: Africa is the only continent crossed by the Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
facts.question: Which continent is crossed by the Equator and both tropics?

facts.title: Largest island
facts.statement: Greenland is the world's largest island at about 2.16 million square kilometres. Australia is larger but is classed as a continent.
facts.question: What is the largest island in the world?
facts.hook: Map projections make it look continent-sized; it is roughly the area of Saudi Arabia and Iran combined.

facts.title: The island shared by three countries
facts.statement: Borneo is the only island divided among three countries: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
facts.question: Which island is shared by three countries?

facts.title: The world's fourth-largest island
facts.statement: Madagascar, off the southeast coast of Africa, is the fourth-largest island and home to species found nowhere else, including all the world's lemurs.
facts.question: Which island nation lies off the southeast coast of Africa?

facts.title: Japan's largest island
facts.statement: Honshu is Japan's largest island and holds Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto — about 80% of the country's population.
facts.question: What is the largest island of Japan?

facts.title: The strait between Europe and Africa
facts.statement: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain from Morocco and is the only natural connection between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.
facts.question: Which strait separates Europe from Africa at the Mediterranean's western end?
facts.hook: At its narrowest it is only about 13 km wide.

facts.title: The strait through Istanbul
facts.statement: The Bosporus runs through Istanbul, separating Europe from Asia and connecting the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.
facts.question: Which strait divides Istanbul between Europe and Asia?

facts.title: The canal joining the Atlantic and Pacific
facts.statement: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, cuts through Central America and saves ships the 13,000 km voyage around South America.
facts.question: Which canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans?

facts.title: The canal joining the Mediterranean and Red Sea
facts.statement: The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea and carries roughly 12% of global trade.
facts.question: Which canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea?

facts.title: The strait between Asia and North America
facts.statement: The Bering Strait separates Russia from Alaska by about 82 km, and was dry land during the last ice age.
facts.question: Which strait separates Russia from Alaska?

facts.title: Most populous city
facts.statement: Tokyo's metropolitan area is the largest urban agglomeration on Earth, with roughly 37 million people.
facts.question: What is the world's most populous metropolitan area?

facts.title: The city on two continents
facts.statement: Istanbul is the only major city spanning two continents, with districts on both the European and Asian sides of the Bosporus.
facts.question: Which major city lies on two continents?

facts.title: Highest capital city
facts.statement: La Paz, Bolivia, is the highest seat of government in the world, sitting at around 3,600 m above sea level.
facts.question: Which city is the world's highest seat of government?

facts.title: Northernmost capital
facts.statement: Reykjavík, Iceland, is the northernmost capital city of any sovereign state, and is heated almost entirely by geothermal energy.
facts.question: What is the world's northernmost capital city?

facts.title: The city built on a lagoon
facts.statement: Venice is built across 118 small islands in a lagoon, its buildings resting on millions of wooden piles driven into the mud.
facts.question: Which Italian city is built on 118 islands in a lagoon?

facts.title: Currency of Japan
facts.statement: The yen is the currency of Japan and the third most traded currency in the world after the US dollar and the euro.
facts.question: What is the currency of Japan?

facts.title: Currency of India
facts.statement: The rupee is the currency of India; the name comes from the Sanskrit rupya, meaning wrought silver.
facts.question: What is the currency of India?
facts.details:
The Indian rupee (symbol: ₹; code: INR) is the official currency of India and the erstwhile British Raj. The rupee is subdivided into 100 paise (singular: paisa). The issuance of the currency is controlled by the Reserve Bank of India. The Reserve Bank derives this role from powers vested in it by the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. It is the world's eleventh-most-traded currency as of April 2025.


== Etymology ==
Pāṇini (6th to 4th century BCE), the ancient Indian grammarian and logician, writes of the rūpya (रूप्य). While it is unclear whether Pāṇini was referring specifically to coinage, some scholars conclude that
he uses the term rūpa to mean a piece of precious metal (typically silver) used as a coin, and a rūpya to mean a stamped piece of metal, a coin in the modern sense. The Arthashastra, written by Chanakya, prime minister to the first Maurya emperor Chandragupta Maurya (c. 340–290 BCE), mentions silver coins as rūpyarūpa. Other types of coins, including gold coins (suvarṇarūpa), copper coins (tāmrarūpa), and lead coins (sīsarūpa), are also mentioned. The immediate precursor to the rupee is the rūpiya—the silver coin weighing 178 grains minted in northern India, first by Sher Shah Suri during his brief rule between 1540 and 1545, and later by the Mughal Empire.

facts.title: Currency of Switzerland
facts.statement: The Swiss franc is the currency of Switzerland and Liechtenstein, and is treated worldwide as a safe-haven currency.
facts.question: What is the currency of Switzerland?
facts.hook: Switzerland is in Europe but not in the euro.

facts.title: Currency of Russia
facts.statement: The ruble is the currency of Russia and one of the oldest national currencies still in use, dating back to the 13th century.
facts.question: What is the currency of Russia?

facts.title: Currency of South Korea
facts.statement: The won is the currency of South Korea; North Korea uses a separate currency of the same name.
facts.question: What is the currency of South Korea?

facts.title: Smallest continent
facts.statement: Australia is the smallest continent by land area, at about 8.6 million square kilometres.
facts.question: What is the smallest continent by land area?

facts.title: The continent of the Amazon
facts.statement: South America holds the Amazon rainforest, the Andes — the world's longest mountain range — and the driest desert on Earth.
facts.question: Which continent contains the Amazon rainforest and the Andes?

facts.title: Second-smallest continent
facts.statement: Europe is the second-smallest continent by area, larger only than Australia, yet holds around 10% of the world's population.
facts.question: Which is the second-smallest continent by land area?
